pl-l3d38c4-d1e130.summary: Defines lying as speaking against what one thinks, whether true or not. Everyone who tells a lie lies, speaking against his mind with will to deceive; but not everyone who lies tells a lie, since sometimes he says what is true while lying, as conversely one may say something false and be truthful.
claims: Lying is speaking against one's mind.
One can lie while saying something true.

pl-l3d38c4-d1e134.summary: Quotes Augustine: no one who says a falsehood he thinks true is lying, since he is deceived, not deceiving; one who says something true he thinks false lies, since he does not say what he thinks; nor is one free of lying who speaks truth unknowingly while willing to deceive.
claims: Saying a falsehood one believes true is not lying.
Saying a truth one believes false is lying.

pl-l3d38c4-d1e143.summary: Asks whether a Jew who says Christ is God without believing it tells a lie.

pl-l3d38c4-d1e146.summary: Answers that what he says is not a lie, since, though he holds otherwise in his mind, what he says is true; yet he lies in saying what is true.
claims: A true statement made insincerely is not a lie.
One can lie while saying what is true.

pl-l3d38c4.summary: Defines lying as speaking against what one thinks, whether it is true or not. So everyone who tells a lie lies, but not everyone who lies tells a lie, since one may lie while saying something true. Augustine: one who says a falsehood he believes true is deceived, not lying, while one who says a truth he thinks false lies. Hence a Jew who says Christ is God without believing it does not tell a lie, since what he says is true, but he lies.
claims: Lying is speaking against what one thinks.
Every one who tells a lie lies, but not every one who lies tells a lie.
Saying a falsehood one believes true is not lying.
Saying a truth one believes false is lying.
